To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the VDR·RXRs complex is a high-affinity and specific heterodimer that binds with high specificity to the VDRES of osteopontin, osteocalcin and other vitamin D-regulated genes; 2) the VDR homodimers bind with much lower affinity to the VDREEs; 3) 1,25(OH)2D3 enhances VDR-RXR heterodimer binding to VDREEs by increasing the stability

the 1,25-dihyroxyvitamin D ligand for the vitamin D receptor is an allosteric regulator that enhances heterodimeric DNA binding by the receptor and its retinoid X partner, whereas 9-cis retinoic acid inhibits heterodimeric VDR-RXR binding.

9-cis retinoic acid inhibits the heterodimeric binding of the vitamin d receptor and retinoid x receptor to the vitamin d response element, whereas 1,25-dihyroxyvitamin D promotes heterodimeric VDR/RXR binding and restricts the action of 9-csi retinoic acid on the VDR/RXR complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular function of vitamin D and its metabolites in the regulation of osteopontin, osteocalcin, and other genes in osteoblasts.
the mechanism of vitamin D action in bone and the role of the vitamin D nuclear receptor in the control of bone metabolism.
the molecular basis of the interaction of the vitamin D hormone with its receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1,25- (OH)2D and RXR ligands act in concert to regulate VDRE-dependent transcriptional activation by VDR.

VDR is an allosteric receptor that can be activated by 1,α,25-diohydroxyvitamin D, which then facilitates the formation of a VDR·RXR heterodimer that can then bind to the osteopontin or osteocalcin vitamin-D-response elements.
the molecular function of the 1,25-dihydrxyvitamin D ligand in the VDR·RXRs complex is to enhance the affinity of the heterodimer for the VDRE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vitamin D and retinoid systems are linked by a common molecular mechanism that may provide a framework to explain the diverse biological functions of the two families of retinoid receptors.
9-cis retinoic acid and 1,25-dihdroxyvitamin D interact to control the activity of the vitamin D and retinoid signaling pathways.
1,25(OH)2D3 and 9-cIS-RA are ligands that modulate the function of VDR and RXR in a manner that is dependent upon their prior interaction with these nuclear receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the VDR and RXR heterodimer is the primary functional receptor complex for 1,25-dihydoxyvitamin D, and that this complex is stabilized by 1, 25-dihydrovyvitamin D and inhibited by 9-ciss-retinoic acid, which may be important for regulating the expression of genes that are involved in bone mineralization.
the VDR·RXRa complex is a functional unit, and that 1,25(OH)2D3 and RXR ligand binding are interdependent processes that can be modulated by 1, 25-(OH) 2D3 and/or 9-cis retinoic acid concentrations.
the molecular action of the 1,25-dihydoxyvitamin D is to generate a conformationally restricted VDR·RXRs that is resistant to the action of other ligands.
